title: Idempotent ledger transfers with client retries
name: Ledger transfer service

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how long this system remembers idempotency keys relative to how clients retry? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A transfer fails with InsufficientFunds. The customer later deposits money and the client retries with the same key within two minutes. What happens?
choices: The transfer is attempted again and may now succeed
An exception propagates to the caller
The key is rejected as a duplicate with an error status
The stored rejection is returned and no transfer is attempted

questions.prompt: Which property of Ledger.transfer matters for two concurrent transfers from the same source account?
choices: Each transfer uses its own lock, so they run in parallel
The balance check and both updates happen under one lock, so the balance cannot be overdrawn by interleaving
The check is outside the lock, so overdrafts are possible
The lock is released before the entry is recorded

questions.prompt: Two simultaneous calls arrive with the same new key and payload. What does TransferService do?
choices: The service lock serializes them, so the second finds the stored result and replays it
Both execute the transfer, since the cache is only written afterwards
The second is rejected with a conflict status
The second waits on the ledger lock and then moves the money again
